subject: Cognitive Science
title: Syntax: The Rules We Never Learned
description: A quick, practical guide to Syntax: The Rules We Never Learned.

hook.text: 'The dog bit the man' means something very different from 'The man bit the dog.' Order creates meaning.

buildup.text: Syntax is the set of rules for ordering words. You know them perfectly but can't state them explicitly.

discovery.text: You can instantly tell that 'Colorless green ideas sleep furiously' is grammatical but meaningless.

twist.text: No one teaches you syntax through lessons. Children extract rules from examples by age three—without instruction.

climax.text: Chomsky argued this means syntax must be partly innate—a universal grammar wired into the human brain.

punchline.text: You follow rules you were never taught.

quiz.question: What did Chomsky argue about syntax?
options: It's partly innate in the brain
